points.title: Why programs use a database
points.must: States that script variables are lost after each run, so data is kept in a database to persist and be shared, searched and updated.
points.model: A script's variables disappear when it finishes (it runs once per request). To keep data between requests, users and days, the program stores it in a database and reads it back. Database = organised, persistent collection of related data in tables (records, fields).

points.title: DBMS
points.must: Definition: software that stores/manages the database and runs the SQL sent to it; examples.
points.model: DBMS = software that stores and manages the database and runs the SQL statements sent to it, e.g. MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite. The program never edits the data files directly — it sends SQL to the DBMS.

points.title: Three tiers
points.must: Browser (form, pages) → web server script (reads, validates, builds SQL, outputs HTML) → database server (tables). Only the script talks to the DB.
points.model: 1) Browser (client): shows pages and forms. 2) Web server: runs the script (PHP) — reads form data, validates, builds and sends SQL, checks result, outputs HTML. 3) Database server (DBMS): holds the tables, runs SQL, returns true/false or rows. The browser never talks to the database directly; the DB password stays on the server.

points.title: Table Student and data types
points.must: The example table with fields, types and the auto-increment primary key; text in quotes, numbers without, DATE as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
points.model: Student(StudentID INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR(50), Grade INT, City VARCHAR(30), BirthDate DATE). Primary key = unique value identifying each record; AUTO_INCREMENT → the DBMS creates it, so INSERT leaves it out.

points.title: Connecting to the database
points.must: mysqli_connect(server, user, password, database); if it fails stop with die() and mysqli_connect_error(); set charset; connect.php included with require.

points.title: Five steps of a database script
points.must: Connect → prepare SQL → run/execute → check/process result → close.
points.model: 1) Connect (stop with error if it fails). 2) Prepare the SQL (INSERT to add, SELECT to extract) using the input values. 3) Run/execute it (mysqli_query or a prepared statement). 4) Check/process the result (success/error message; loop through rows). 5) Close: mysqli_close($conn).

points.title: Same steps in Python
points.must: Comparison PHP mysqli vs Python sqlite3, including conn.commit() / transaction.
points.model: Python: conn = sqlite3.connect("school.db"); conn.execute("INSERT INTO Student (Name, Grade) VALUES (?, ?)", (n, g)); conn.commit(); cur.lastrowid; conn.close(). commit() saves a transaction (group of changes saved together or not at all); MySQL autocommits.

points.title: INSERT statement and its forms
points.must: Definition and the three forms: all fields in order, named fields (recommended), several records; field count = value count; unlisted fields get default/NULL.

points.title: Writing values in SQL
points.must: Text and dates in single quotes, numbers without, date 'YYYY-MM-DD', NULL without quotes; apostrophe problem.
points.model: Text: 'Astana'. Number: 11, 1250.50 (no quotes). Date: '2009-03-14'. Boolean: TRUE/FALSE. No value: NULL. An apostrophe inside text (O'Brien) ends the text early and breaks the SQL.

points.title: Building the SQL from variables and checking the result
points.must: Double-quoted string with '$name' and $grade; echo $sql to debug; mysqli_query true/false; mysqli_insert_id, mysqli_affected_rows, mysqli_error.

points.title: Form field → variable → column
points.must: name attribute → $_POST key → variable (trim, (int)) → column in INSERT; values arrive as text.
points.model: <input name="year"> → $_POST["year"] ("2008", text) → $year = (int)$_POST["year"] → column Year (INT). The same name links each step; a spelling mistake breaks the chain. Example: INSERT INTO Book (Title, Author, Year, Copies) VALUES ('Abai Zholy', 'Mukhtar Auezov', 1942, 5).

points.title: UPDATE and DELETE need WHERE
points.must: UPDATE … SET … WHERE and DELETE FROM … WHERE; without WHERE every record changes.

points.title: Validation before INSERT
points.must: Definition; checks presence, type, range, length, format, lookup with examples; collect errors in an array; server-side is compulsory because client-side can be bypassed.
points.model:
Validation = automatic check that data is sensible (present, right type, in range, right length/format) before it is stored; it cannot prove data is correct.
Presence $name !== ""; type is_numeric(); range 7–12; length strlen($name) <= 50; format preg_match('/^\+7\d{10}$/'); lookup in_array($city, [...]).
Client-side (HTML required/min/max, JS) is instant but can be bypassed; server-side validation in the script protects the database.

points.title: SQL injection
points.must: Definition and how it works: input joined into the SQL string, quote closes text, extra statement, -- comments out the rest.
points.model:
SQL injection = the user types SQL code into an input; when the program joins the input into its SQL string, the code becomes part of the statement and is executed.
Input x', 0); DELETE FROM Student; -- gives
INSERT INTO Student (Name, Grade) VALUES ('x', 0); DELETE FROM Student; --', 11)
Cause: data and code mixed in one string.

points.title: Prepared statements
points.must: Definition; prepare → bind (type letters s, i, d, b) → execute; input always treated as data; full safe code; htmlspecialchars on output.
